name: UCC2891DR
title: UCC2891/2/3/4: current-mode active-clamp PWM controllers with complementary clamp-switch driver
summary: A family of four fixed-frequency, peak current-mode PWM controllers for active-clamp forward and flyback converters. Each drives the main N-channel switch (OUT) and the clamp switch (AUX) with 2-A outputs and a resistor-set dead time between them, and adds programmable slope compensation, a precise maximum duty cycle, a synchronizable oscillator to 1 MHz, soft-start with soft stop, pulse skipping of both outputs and an accurate line monitor. The UCC2891/3 include a 110-V JFET start-up regulator on pin 16; the UCC2892/4 use pin 16 for line overvoltage. AUX is active-low for a P-channel clamp (UCC2891/2) or active-high for an N-channel clamp (UCC2893/4). The UCC2891DR is the UCC2891 in SOIC-16 on tape and reel.
key_figures: 18 V to 110 V recommended, 120 V absolute
2 A source, 2 A sink, OUT and AUX
250 kHz typ at RON = ROFF = 75 kΩ; up to 1.0 MHz

notes: The four devices differ in two ways: the AUX output drives a P-channel clamp switch (UCC2891, UCC2892) or an N-channel one (UCC2893, UCC2894), and pin 16 is the high-voltage start-up input VIN (UCC2891, UCC2893) or the line overvoltage input LINEOV (UCC2892, UCC2894). The current-sense threshold is 0.75 V on the parts with the start-up circuit and 1.27 V on the others.
An R suffix orders tape and reel: 2,500 per reel in the D package, 2,000 in the PW package. Tubes hold 40 (D) or 90 (PW).

pins.package: SOIC-16 (D) and TSSOP-16 (PW), UCC2891 and UCC2893

pins.name: RTDEL
pins.function: A resistor to GND sets the turn-on delay between the two gate outputs (the dead time between OUT and AUX in both directions). The pin sits at about 2.5 V DC internally; the same resistor also sets the line-monitor hysteresis current.

pins.name: RTON
pins.function: A resistor to GND sets the current that charges the internal timing capacitor, and with it the on-time part of the oscillator period. The soft-start current is also derived from this resistor. Held at about 2.5 V internally.

pins.name: RTOFF
pins.function: A resistor to GND sets the current that discharges the internal timing capacitor. Together with RTON it fixes the switching period and the maximum duty cycle. Held at about 2.5 V internally.

pins.name: VREF
pins.function: 5-V reference and internal logic supply. It can source about 5 mA to outside circuits and is current limited. Needs a ceramic capacitor to GND close to the pin: 0.22 µF recommended, 0.022 µF minimum for stability, about 22 µF maximum. Present only while UVLO allows operation; its rise is not necessarily monotonic before VDD reaches 5 V.

pins.name: SYNC
pins.function: One-way clock input for synchronizing the oscillator. The rising edge ends the timing-capacitor charge period. The external clock must run faster than the free-running oscillator, and the pulse must be at least about 50 ns wide and shorter than (1 - DMAX) × TSYNC so that the programmed maximum duty cycle holds.

pins.name: GND
pins.function: Reference ground for the small-signal control and programming circuits. Not joined to PGND inside; connect it to PGND with one direct link at the device.

pins.name: CS
pins.function: Feeds the current-limit and PWM comparators. Feed it from the current-sense resistor through an RC filter (RF, CF), never directly across the resistor: the slope-compensation current flows out of this pin through RF, and an internal pull-down discharges the pin during the guaranteed off time. Pulse-by-pulse limiting starts near 0.75 V on the UCC2891/3 and 1.27 V on the UCC2892/4.

pins.name: RSLOPE
pins.function: A resistor to GND sets the size of the slope-compensation current. During the OUT on-time the voltage on this pin copies the timing-capacitor ramp, so the pin carries a fast AC waveform; keep stray capacitance and inductance on this node low.

pins.name: FB
pins.function: Control-voltage input of the PWM, normally driven by an optocoupler from a secondary-side error amplifier, with a pull-up resistor to VREF. Usable range about 1.25 V to 4.5 V: below 1.25 V the duty cycle is zero (pulses are skipped), above 4.5 V it is DMAX.

pins.name: SS/SD
pins.function: Soft-start capacitor to GND. Charged by a DC current set by RON; its buffered voltage and FB are compared and the lower one controls the PWM. Discharged by a matching current during a fault. Pulling it below about 0.5 V shuts the controller down.

pins.name: PGND
pins.function: Return for the OUT and AUX drivers and the other high-current bias circuits. Keep the loop from the outputs to the switches and back short and small in area. Join to GND externally, between pins 6 and 11.

pins.name: AUX
pins.function: Gate drive for the auxiliary (active-clamp) switch, 2 A source and 2 A sink; it is on while the main switch is off. Active low for a P-channel clamp switch on the UCC2891 and UCC2892, active high for an N-channel one on the UCC2893 and UCC2894.

pins.name: OUT
pins.function: Active-high gate drive for the main N-channel MOSFET, 2 A source and 2 A sink. A 10-kΩ resistor from this pin to PGND is recommended.

pins.name: VDD
pins.function: Supply for the gate drivers, the internal 5-V regulator and part of the UVLO circuit. Place a 1-µF ceramic capacitor (CHF) close between VDD and PGND, at least ten times the VREF capacitor, and a larger storage capacitor (CBIAS) beside it. In steady state power comes from a bootstrap winding or an auxiliary supply. With the internal JFET doing start-up, the load on VDD must stay under 4 mA.

pins.name: LINEUV
pins.function: Line undervoltage input. A divider from the input voltage brings it to the 1.27-V threshold; crossing it upward enables the outputs, and an internal current set by RDEL then flows out of the pin into the lower divider resistor to give hysteresis on the way down.

pins.name: VIN
pins.function: High-voltage start-up input, tied straight to the input rail when the input stays within the 110-V rating. An internal P-channel JFET charges the VDD capacitors with about 15 mA until VDD reaches the UVLO turn-on level, and is off whenever the gate drivers are switching.

circuits.title: Simplified application: active-clamp forward converter with synchronous rectifiers
circuits.description: U1 runs a forward converter. Q1 is the main switch on the low end of the primary with RCS in its source; its current reaches CS through RF, and CF to GND filters it. A low-side P-channel clamp switch Q2 and CCLAMP sit across the primary switch node; AUX drives Q2 through CAUX, with DAUX and a gate resistor to ground restoring the level, so Q2's gate swings below ground. RIN1 and RIN2 set the line undervoltage level on LINEUV, CBULK holds the input, and VIN is tied to the input for start-up. After start-up a bias winding feeds VDD through a diode, with CBIAS as storage. On the secondary Q3 and Q4 rectify under an SR drive block, Lo and Co filter the output, and a secondary-side error amplifier closes the loop to FB across the isolation barrier. The timing, delay, slope and soft-start parts hang from their pins to GND.

parts.note: power transformer; P1 dotted primary end, P2 other primary end, S1 dotted secondary end, S2 other secondary end
SR drive block; G3 and G4 drive Q3 and Q4
secondary-side error amplifier; VO senses the output, FB drives U1 across the isolation

notes: The error amplifier's link to FB crosses the isolation barrier; the secondary return SGND is separate from the primary ground.

circuits.title: Typical setup, UCC2891 and UCC2893
circuits.description: The controller's own parts around a power stage drawn as a block. RDEL, RON, ROFF and RSLOPE go from their pins to GND and set the dead time, the oscillator charge and discharge currents, and the slope compensation; CVREF bypasses VREF and CSS sets soft-start. RF and CF filter the power stage's current signal into CS. RVREF pulls FB up to VREF and the optocoupler's transistor pulls it down. CHF and CBIAS sit on VDD to PGND, and ROT holds OUT low. RIN1 and RIN2 scale the input onto LINEUV, and VIN takes the input rail for start-up. Part values follow from the design equations.

parts.note: optocoupler output transistor, C collector and E emitter; its LED is on the isolated feedback side
power stage block: VIN and RTN its input rails, OUT and AUX its two gate inputs, CS its current-sense output

notes: GND (pin 6) and PGND (pin 11) are joined by a single link between the two pins, next to the controller.

circuits.title: Zero voltage switching flyback with high-side N-channel clamp
circuits.description: An active-clamp flyback. QMAIN switches the low end of the primary with RCS in its source wired straight to CS, and ROT holds OUT low. The clamp is on the high side: CCLAMP from the input rail in series with the N-channel QAUX to the switch node, the gate fed from AUX through an N-channel gate drive block. The secondary charges COUT through a synchronous rectifier in its return leg, run by its own control block. A secondary-side error amplifier with isolation drives FB. VIN connects to the input, and a bootstrap bias block supplies VDD with CBIAS. The active clamp lets the primary switches turn on at zero voltage.

circuits.title: Active clamp forward converter with low-side P-channel clamp
circuits.description: An active-clamp forward converter. QMAIN switches the low end of the primary with RCS in its source wired straight to CS. The clamp is on the low side: CCLAMP from the switch node in series with the P-channel QAUX to -VIN, the gate fed from AUX through a P-channel gate drive block. On the secondary, SR1 rectifies in the winding return and SR2 freewheels the output inductor LO into COUT, both run by a control block. A secondary-side error amplifier with isolation drives FB; VIN connects to the input, and a bootstrap bias block supplies VDD with CBIAS.

circuits.title: High-side N-channel clamp gate drive (UCC2893/4)
circuits.description: AUX drives a small gate-drive transformer T2 through a series capacitor C1 and resistor R1, the primary returned to power ground. The secondary, referenced to the switch node, couples through C2; D1 and R2 restore the DC level across the clamp switch's gate and source. D2 charges the gate of the high-side N-channel QAUX, and the PNP Q1, its base on the restored node, discharges the gate for a fast turn-off. QAUX in series with CCLAMP clamps the switch node to the input rail. The transformer must pass any duty cycle from 1 - DMAX to nearly 1.

parts.note: gate-drive transformer; P1 dotted primary end, P2 other, S1 dotted secondary end, S2 other
power transformer primary; P1 to +VIN, P2 to the switch node

circuits.title: Low-side P-channel clamp gate drive (UCC2891/2)
circuits.description: AUX drives the gate of the low-side P-channel clamp switch QAUX through C1. D1 from the gate to ground and R1 across it shift the level, so the gate swings from about ground down to minus the drive amplitude whatever the duty cycle. QAUX in series with CCLAMP connects the switch node to ground through the clamp capacitor.

parts.note: power transformer primary; P1 to +VIN, P2 to the switch node

circuits.title: Bootstrap bias from a transformer winding, flyback example
circuits.description: An extra winding on the flyback transformer feeds VDD through a diode into CBIAS. Because the output is regulated and the winding voltage follows the output by the turns ratio, VDD is regulated too. The rest is the flyback power path: QMAIN on the primary, a synchronous rectifier with its control block on the secondary, the output capacitor and the load.

parts.note: transformer; P1 dotted primary end, P2 other; S1 dotted secondary end, S2 other; B1 dotted bias winding end, B2 other

circuits.title: Bootstrap bias from the output inductor, forward example
circuits.description: In a forward converter a winding on the main transformer would follow the input voltage, so the bias is taken instead from a winding coupled to the output inductor. During freewheeling the inductor carries the regulated output voltage, and its coupled winding feeds VDD through a diode into CBIAS. The power path is a forward converter with QMAIN on the primary and two synchronous rectifiers on the secondary.

notes: The bias voltage in both bootstrap schemes follows the output, so under heavy overload or a short the bias falls below UVLO and the converter runs in hiccup mode.

circuits.title: UCC2891EVM: 36-72 V input, 3.3 V output active-clamp forward converter
circuits.description: A complete telecom-input forward converter. The input bulk C1, C2, C4 feeds T2's paralleled primaries through the primary of current transformer T1. Q2 is the main switch driven from OUT through R10, with D3 across it for a quick turn-off; the low-side P-channel Q1 and C9 form the active clamp, Q1's gate driven from AUX through R4 and C6 with D2 and R8 setting the level. T1's secondary, rectified by D1 into R9 and C8 with R7 as its reset path, gives the current signal that reaches CS through R6, filtered by C5. R1, R2, R3 and R5 program dead time, on-time, off-time and slope; C3 bypasses VREF and C7 sets soft-start; R11 and R12 divide the input onto LINEUV, and VIN takes the input for start-up. The secondary uses self-driven rectifiers: Q3 and Q4 driven from the opposite winding end through R14 and R15, and Q5, Q7, Q8 freewheeling through L1 into C17, C20, C21. A winding on L1 rectified by D8 into C19 supplies VDD (P_BIAS), with C10 and C11 as storage. On the secondary, D4 and D5 rectify the winding into R16 and C12, and Q6 with zener D6 makes a local supply for the optocoupler U2 through R17. The TLV431 D7 compares the output, divided by R25, R26 and R27, with its reference and pulls the optocoupler LED, with R21, C15 and C16 as compensation; the optocoupler pulls FB against R13 from VREF. Q9 with R28, R29, C22 and D9 shapes the start-up of the feedback divider. R24 between J7 and J8 is an injection point for loop measurement.

operation.text: The UCC2891, UCC2892, UCC2893 and UCC2894 are fixed-frequency peak current-mode PWM controllers for active-clamp (active-reset) forward and flyback converters. Besides the main gate drive OUT they have a complementary AUX drive for the clamp switch with a programmable turn-on delay between the two. The UCC2891/3 add a 110-V start-up regulator; the UCC2892/4 use that pin for line overvoltage instead. Target uses are 150-W to 700-W supplies, off-line and DC-DC, including 48-V telecom, server, datacom, high-power adapters and flat-panel TV supplies.

At power-up the internal JFET from VIN charges CBIAS and CHF on VDD. At about 12.7 V the UVLO enables the controller, the JFET turns off and VREF comes up to 5 V. Switching starts only when VREF is above 4.5 V, CS is below the current limit, FB is above 1.25 V and the input is between the line UV and OV levels. Until the bootstrap winding takes over, the controller runs from CBIAS, so CBIAS must hold VDD above the turn-off threshold (about 8 V) for the whole start-up, or the supply goes through repeated restart attempts. In steady state VDD can be anywhere between the UVLO turn-off level and the recommended maximum. The JFET cannot carry the full operating load including gate drive; it serves start-up and stand-by only.

When switching is suspended on command, the bootstrap winding gives no power. The JFET then holds VDD up as long as the outputs stay off: it turns on at VDD = 10 V, charges CBIAS to about 13.5 V and turns off again, repeating. On re-enable the controller is already biased and goes straight to soft-start; once gate pulses appear the JFET stays off and bias must come from the bootstrap circuit.

Switching may continue until VDD falls below the UVLO turn-off level (about 8 V). The controller then shuts down completely, VREF goes off, and it returns to the start-up state with the JFET charging CBIAS again; if the input is present it tries to restart.

With bootstrap bias, falling input ends operation through the line UV comparator. Near minimum input the duty cycle approaches DMAX and the clamp capacitor voltage is at its highest, and that voltage could remain long after switching stops; a soft-start into it could saturate the transformer. To avoid this the controller keeps OUT and AUX switching while CSS discharges slowly, so the pulse widths and the clamp voltage fall together (soft stop of both outputs).

When LINEOV trips, both gate drives stop at once and CSS starts its slow discharge, with the drives held off. When VSS has reached 0.5 V and the overvoltage has gone, the converter restarts through a normal soft-start.

When FB falls below the zero-duty boundary of 1.25 V a main pulse is skipped, and the matching AUX pulse is skipped too. This keeps the clamp switch from holding the clamp voltage across the transformer for several cycles, which avoids reverse saturation and keeps the clamp capacitor voltage.

The oscillator limits the maximum duty cycle by timing the charge and discharge of an internal capacitor separately: OUT can be on only while the capacitor charges and is always off while it is reset. A rising edge on SYNC ends the charge and starts the discharge; the next charge begins when the valley is reached, so both slopes and hence DMAX stay as programmed. The sync clock must be faster than the free-running frequency and may be in phase or out of phase for interleaving. The pulse must be wider than about 50 ns and narrower than (1 - DMAX) × TSYNC; a wider pulse adds a flat part to the timing waveform with both outputs off, which does not suit an active-clamp converter and is not recommended. With SYNC held high both outputs stay off. The oscillator runs up to 1.0 MHz.

CSS charges from 0 V to about 5 V at ISS, but only the span from 1.25 V to 4.5 V controls the PWM, so CSS is sized on that span. The soft-start interval is the time to reach full current capability, not the output ramp time; the output's rise also depends on the current limit, output capacitance and load. For a controlled output ramp, ramp the reference of the secondary error amplifier instead (closed-loop soft-start).

CS feeds the PWM and current-limit comparators through an RC filter RF, CF. CF goes from CS to GND, 50 pF to 270 pF, and is kept small so it does not filter the slope current. Slope compensation is a current sourced out of CS that rises linearly during the OUT on-time and develops a ramp across RF; RSLOPE sets its size. The CS pin is pulled down internally during the timing-capacitor discharge, the guaranteed off time of (1 - DMAX) × TSW. The FB voltage is buffered and divided down to the current-sense level inside.

The controller design starts from the finished power stage: switching frequency, maximum duty cycle, soft-start time, the gate charges of both MOSFETs, the bias method and voltage, the required turn-on delay, the turn-on, turn-off and overvoltage input levels with the overvoltage hysteresis, and the reflected down-slope of the output inductor current at the sense resistor.

GND and PGND are separate inside. Give the small-signal parts (the optocoupler emitter, CSS, RSLOPE, CF, CVREF and the RDEL, RON, ROFF resistors) a ground area of their own, joined to the power ground at a single point between pins 6 and 11. Place the controller close to the MOSFETs and connect OUT and AUX to the gates with wide, overlapping traces to keep gate-loop inductance low. Keep the RSLOPE node free of parasitic capacitance and inductance. CHF goes directly between VDD and PGND.

Either topology can use a high-side or a low-side clamp. A high-side N-channel clamp switch (UCC2893/4) needs a high-side driver IC or a gate-drive transformer; the transformer must handle any clamp duty cycle from 1 - DMAX to nearly 1. A low-side P-channel clamp switch (UCC2891/2) is driven through a capacitor and diode level shifter, which keeps the gate amplitude independent of duty cycle.

In a flyback, an extra winding on the transformer gives a quasi-regulated VDD: the output voltage scaled by the winding turns ratio. In a forward converter a winding on the main transformer follows the input voltage and could exceed the controller's maximum at high line; a linear regulator can limit it, or the bias can be taken from a winding on the output inductor, which sees the regulated output during freewheeling. In both cases the bias tracks the output, so under heavy overload or short circuit it drops below UVLO and the converter runs in hiccup mode.

The active-clamp topologies let the primary switches turn on at zero voltage, which cuts switching loss and allows a higher switching frequency or better efficiency than a hard-switched design at the same frequency.
ESD protection inside the part is limited. Keep the pins shorted together, or the part in conductive foam, while it is stored or handled.
